prior_pilot_publication.scope: Prior failed pilot is development exposure; its weights are not the new initialization.

training.initialization: Identical frozen v3 parameters; fresh zero Adam and update count; sampling RNG explicitly reset after construction.
training.endpoint: Fixed episode 4096, 256 full batches; no internal validation, best checkpoint selection, early stopping, or resume.
training.experience_pairing: Same scenario seeds and initial actor RNG; identical first batch trajectories required. Later trajectories may diverge.
training.normalization: Reference advantages are undiscounted return-to-go minus ordinary sampled learned-critic values. If n>1 and reference std>1e-8, apply (advantage-reference mean)/(reference std+1e-8); otherwise use raw advantages. Never recenter the substituted vector.
training.anchored_baseline: Keep the ordinary critic baseline for the first decision; substitute an independent paired STOP reward-to-go only after an existing placement. Ordinary values remain separately available for reference normalization.
training.rationale: Four thousand ninety-six live episodes per arm gives the new credit rule a meaningful further learning horizon. Chosen before accessing any new training or validation scenario.

validation.confidence_interval: Two-sided 95% percentile intervals from paired case resampling within each profile, then the equally weighted mean of three profile means.
validation.prior_pilot_comparison: all_step_stop_pilot is the frozen prior 1024-episode endpoint, not a matched 4096-episode training control.

scale_gate.interpretation: Every condition must hold against both comparators. Point guards are not statistical noninferiority. Passing only authorizes multi-seed replication, not promotion. Shared-critic, prior policies and greedy remain reported references; cost or return alone cannot pass.

diagnostics: Exact identical first-batch feature/mask/action/reward trajectory digest across all arms.
First-decision applied coefficients equal ordinary reference-normalized coefficients on each actual batch, including STOP; no claim of equal gradients or future stopping behavior.
Ordinary/applied raw and normalized credit, return-to-go and both baselines by first/later and STOP/deployment.
Clipping, gradient norms, critic-head invariants, sensor and profile counts, learning curves, live decisions, later-only branch counts, and measured compute.
Paired timely sensing, all-threat success, detection, return and cost; descriptive initial STOP flips and later-layout changes.
limitations: Single training seed. Scenario confidence intervals do not measure training-seed uncertainty.
This remains the existing sampled, transition-averaged optimizer with a batch-dependent scale; it is not claimed to be an exactly unbiased policy-gradient estimator.
Shared parameters and diverging trajectories can change initial decisions despite preserving first-decision credit on an identical batch.
Paired STOP uses private simulator reward only in detached training records, never actor observations or external-input inference. It is not an oracle optimal-STOP label.
The diagnostic prior all-step pilot differs in training seed and duration; its comparison cannot isolate the changed baseline rule.

Synthetic initial sequential sensor type/site planning only. Timely confirmed sensing is not interception. No native Unreal, live sensor, physical command, or mid-flight relocation validation is claimed.
A failed development screen is not proof that the method can never work. Reserved final tests remain unopened.
